title: Java Naming Conventions
content: Classes must be PascalCase (e.g., UserService). Methods and variables must be camelCase (e.g., getUserById). Constants must be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. Packages must be lowercase (e.g., com.autosdlc.service). Avoid abbreviations.

title: Password Storage
content: NEVER store passwords in plaintext. Always use BCryptPasswordEncoder with strength 10 or higher. Password field in DB must be VARCHAR(255) minimum. Never log passwords or return them in API responses.

title: REST Endpoint Naming
content: Use plural nouns and kebab-case. Version your APIs. Examples: GET /api/v1/users, POST /api/v1/users, GET /api/v1/users/{id}. Use nouns, not verbs. Use proper HTTP methods: GET for fetch, POST for create, PUT for full update, PATCH for partial, DELETE for delete.

title: JPA Best Practices
content: Always use FetchType.LAZY for @ManyToOne and @OneToMany to avoid N+1 problem. Use @Transactional on service layer, not controller. Use @Column(name=...) to map snake_case DB columns. Always add created_at, updated_at timestamps. Use UUID for public IDs, Long for internal.

title: Input Validation
content: Always validate request DTOs using Jakarta Validation: @NotNull, @NotBlank, @Size, @Email. Use @Valid on controller method params. Return 400 Bad Request with clear field errors. Never trust client input.

title: Unit Test Standards
content: Follow Given-When-Then pattern. Test class name: ClassNameTest. Use JUnit 5 + Mockito. Mock external dependencies. Aim for 80% coverage on service layer. Each service method must have at least one success and one failure test case.

title: API Response Structure
content: All APIs must return consistent wrapper: {status, message, data, timestamp}. Never return raw entities. Always use DTOs. Use ResponseEntity with proper HTTP status codes. Error response must include errorCode field.

title: SQL Injection Prevention
content: Always use JPA Repositories or Prepared Statements. Never concatenate user input into @Query with String. Use parameterized queries. Validate all inputs before using in queries. Use Spring Data JPA Specifications for dynamic queries.

title: Exception Handling
content: Never use try-catch in controllers. Use @ControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler for global handling. Create custom exceptions like ResourceNotFoundException, BusinessException. Log exception with slf4j logger with proper level. Never swallow exceptions.

title: Logging Standards
content: Use SLF4J with Lombok @Slf4j. Log levels: INFO for business flow, DEBUG for detailed data, ERROR for failures. Never use System.out.println. Include jobId/taskId in MDC for tracing. Log entry and exit of agent executions.

title: Business Requirements Format
content: For BA Agent: Every requirement must have ID (REQ-001), Title, Description, Priority (MUST/SHOULD/COULD), Acceptance Criteria in Gherkin format (Given-When-Then), and related User Story. BRD must contain Project Overview, Scope, Stakeholders, Functional Requirements, Non-Functional Requirements.
